profile.reading: This is an Amazon Web Services data center building located in Tarrant County, Texas, in the Fort Worth metro area. Fort Worth and the wider Dallas-Fort Worth region have become an active hyperscale data center market in recent years, and DataCenterDynamics has reported on AWS filing to develop two new data center campuses in Texas, part of a broader pattern of AWS and other major cloud providers expanding into North Texas for its available land, power infrastructure, and business friendly regulatory environment. The Fort Worth Report, a local nonprofit newsroom, has separately covered the citys growing data center footprint and where new facilities are being sited. As with AWS facilities generally, the company does not publish individual building addresses, capacities, or technical specifications, so this specific buildings construction date, square footage, and critical IT megawattage cannot be independently confirmed from any published source during this research.

profile.disclosure_policy: Confirmed directly on AWS own Global Infrastructure page (aws.amazon.com/about-aws/global-infrastructure/regions_az/): AWS does not publish specific street addresses or per-building technical specifications (square footage, power capacity in MW) for its data centers, as a matter of stated security and operational policy. AWS states each Region consists of a minimum of three isolated, physically separate Availability Zones, each with independent power, cooling, and physical security, but does not break this down to individual facility addresses. This session confirmed this disclosure policy directly rather than assuming it, and applies this finding to AWS records that otherwise have no facility specific address, square footage, planned capacity, or critical_it_mw on file. This is a company wide policy finding, not a statement that no such facility exists at this location.
